status: DRAFT shaped plan by akiendell_cc_0, 2026-11-14, for akienasus to cast. Not cast. Sibling of the inference proxy's charter-verbs ticket.
title: the harbor master's charter names the verb the device answers
intention: The charter's public_interface names each bus verb the device answers (crossing), with the body keys it reads and the reply it gives, so a caller reads the door from the charter and not from the code; each entry is quoted from the handler and, where the outline names the verb, cites the outline line. A verb the device answers and the outline does not name is written in the charter AND listed as a finding for the outline's owner, never blessed by silence.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 (census of every declared_verbs file under cairn/devices): the harbor master's device.py:54 declares one verb, crossing, and its charter has NO public_interface field. RULE 1 says a component is reached through what its charter declares in public_interface; a caller can reach these verbs only by reading the code. The census that found this gap (scratchpad census_verbs2.py, ast read of declared_verbs against the nearest charter's public_interface, 2026-11-14): 5 of 10 declared_verbs files have a gap; the proxy is covered by its own ticket, this is one of the four siblings, and the general sieve is a separate PROPOSED plan to be cast after the move chain lands.
traces_to: RULE 1 (a component is reached through its declared public_interface), Law 5 (intent and code may not contradict), Law 4 (the proof is the instrument).

clauses.claim: every verb key of declared_verbs in cairn/devices/codemother/machines/harbor_master/device.py (ast read, base verbs excluded) appears in the charter's public_interface as "bus verb '<name>'"

each entry names the body keys its handler reads and the reply keys it returns, as the handler reads (quoted below in measured), and an entry for a verb the outline does not name says so in a trailing 'not in the outline' clause
every public_interface entry that existed before is unchanged byte for byte, and a verb the charter names that the device does not declare is a red

decisions.text: D1: public_interface is ADDED as one entry per verb in the form the proxy's 'calls' entry uses ("bus verb 'x' (ticket ...): body {...} -> {...}"); written through the artifact door (cairn artifact write), a field-level diff touching public_interface only. Outline quoted: outline 9.4.1.5: 'VERBS: status queries only (show, get), and crossing, the notice a ...' (the line names crossing; the entry should quote its full text).
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause, red first; it reads the device file with ast and the charter with json, starts no device and imports none.

out: the harbor master's views (map, traffic), which are not verbs

measured.saw: device.py:61 _handle_crossing: body is the crossing notice (reads ticket, component, to); it patches the cached fleet register, counts crossings since reconcile, emits crossing_patched, and replies {accepted: True, verb: 'crossing', device, patched: True}. Views map and traffic are declared separately (declared_views). Charter: public_interface ABSENT. The outline names crossing, so there is no finding here.
measured.how: read cairn/devices/codemother/machines/harbor_master/device.py handlers with python ast (docstrings and bodies) and the outline lines quoted in D1; COLLISION CHECK 2026-11-14 over 101 origin branches: no branch touches this charter. The device code file the proof READS is touched by other branches (see the bounds note), but this ticket never writes it, so it cannot conflict.

unmeasured: reply shapes beyond what the handler returns directly; whether the outline is meant to name the verbs listed as findings
